answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each agent identity must answer randomized micro-challenges drawn from its own prior output (a growing kernel of verified responses); missing one decays its challenge priority. Sustained accuracy costs roughly 40 minutes of compute per identity per day, so a farm of N sybils pays N times that attention, not a one-time fee. A fable spread cheaply by fresh identities fails because unverified newcomers get no challenge history; a falcon-like lurker that skips challenges loses standing.
